name: GNoME (Graph Networks for Materials Exploration)
subcategory: crystal stability prediction and materials discovery
origin_detail: Google DeepMind; predicted structures contributed to the Materials Project (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory).
flagship_projects: GNoME dataset (381,000 stable materials, expanded Aug 2024 to >520,000)

licences.weights: trained weights not released (not mentioned on GitHub or blog)
licences.data: CC BY-NC 4.0; Materials Project copy access-controlled, non-commercial opt-in

openness_notes: Blog (2023-11-29): 2.2 million new crystals predicted, 380,000 most stable; DeepMind 'will contribute' them to the Materials Project. GitHub: code ('Colab notebooks and associated code') Apache-2.0, with JAX NequIP model definitions and 'basic configuration parameters' but no trained weights mentioned. Data CC BY-NC 4.0: 381,000 stable materials, expanded in August 2024 to >520,000 within 1 meV/atom of the hull. In the Materials Project the GNoME records (batch gnome_r2scan_statics) are access-controlled under a separate 'GNoME Database License and Terms of Use', non-commercial and opt-in. The model was 'trained on a snapshot of Materials Project from 2018' (CC BY 4.0). Group I scoring: 0 = no weights; 1 = weights only under non-commercial or gated custom terms; 2 = open code/weights with the flagship model, weights or training data closed (open core); 3 = code and weights under OSI-type or CC BY licences; 4 = 3 plus openly downloadable training data, or outputs published as an open database stewarded by a public institution. Score 1: no weights and non-commercial data.

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 code; CC BY-NC 4.0 data; no weights
Materials Project: GNoME subset access-controlled, non-commercial opt-in

relicensing_events.from: Materials Project content offered under CC BY 4.0
relicensing_events.to: Materials Project with a non-commercial, access-controlled GNoME subset
relicensing_events.outcome_note: A model trained on open CC BY public data contributed its outputs back under non-commercial terms, so the public database is no longer under one licence (see F/materials-project.json). Date not confirmed.

risk_events: Non-commercial data inside a public DOE database
No weights, so predictions cannot be reproduced or extended independently
robustness: Data are mirrored in the Materials Project, but under non-commercial terms; the model itself stays with Google.
physical_science_relevance: Inorganic materials discovery: external researchers 'independently synthesized 736' GNoME-predicted materials, and Berkeley Lab's A-Lab synthesised more than 41 new materials using GNoME stability insights.

training_data.name: Materials Project (2018 snapshot)
training_data.note: Plus active-learning DFT calculations by DeepMind.

openness_effect_assessment: GNoME's predictions spread through the Materials Project, but the non-commercial terms and missing weights limit reuse. Unlike AF2, it did not become a tool others run. The open MLIP ecosystem (MACE, CHGNet, Orb, UMA) instead grew from public data.
key_takeaway: GNoME is the materials-science counterpart of AlphaFold 3's restriction: corporate model, public training data (Materials Project), non-commercial outputs, no weights. It also imported a non-commercial carve-out into a public database.
